summary: Gangzhun is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Qinghai Nationalities University until 1989 and completed a master's degree under Alak Dorje Rinpoche at Northwest Minzu University from 1998 to 2001.

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir studied for an M.Phil at the University of Oslo under MA supervisor Hanna Havnevik, as attested in 2008, and also studied under traditional teacher Lama Byambaa.
Garab Dorje Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Garcin de Tassy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Collège de France under Silvestre de Sacy, Langlès, and Kieffer. A founder of the Société Asiatique, he held the Indian language chair at INALCO from 1828 to 1877.

Gareth Fisher works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. in socio-cultural anthropology from the University of Virginia (1999–2006) and was appointed Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University in 2008.

Gareth Sparham is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and earned a Ph.D. under Ashok Aklujkar at the University of British Columbia, later lecturing at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

Gary A. Tubb is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served on the faculty at Harvard (~1979–1999), Columbia (~1999–2007), and the University of Chicago (~2007–2023), becoming professor emeritus in 2023.

A scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, Gary D. DeAngelis was mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Muhammad Daud Rahbar. He served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at Holy Cross.

Gary Donnelly works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Oxford, Liverpool (MA 2013–2014), and Manchester, later teaching at Liverpool (2016–2020), advising at Manchester (2021), and serving as Lecturer in Indic Traditions at Liverpool Hope University in 2023.

Gary Goh Wee Kian is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under supervisors Hui-Chieh Loy and Jay L. Garfield, as well as teachers Brook Ziporyn, Christopher Anthony Brown, and Cecilia Lim.

Gary Snyder is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley. He trained under traditional teachers including Shunryu Suzuki and served as professor at the University of California, Davis (1986–2002).

Gary Urton is an anthropologist and archaeologist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He taught at Colgate University (1978–2002) and served as Dumbarton Oaks Professor and anthropology chair at Harvard University (~2002–2020).

Gaspare Gorresio was an Italian Indologist who studied under Amedeo Peyron, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He held the Sanskrit chair at the University of Turin from 1852 and served as director of Turin's National University Library.

Gaston Courtillier was an Indologist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot in 1897. He taught at Lycée Fustel de Coulanges (~1919–1933) and lectured in Sanskrit at the University of Strasbourg in 1924.

Gaston Paris was a French linguist who studied under Friedrich Christian Diez and at the École des chartes. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1903) and the Collège de France (1872–1903).
Gaston Renondeau was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Polytechnique from ~1899 to 1901.
Gaton Ngawang Lekpa was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Gauri Viswanathan is an Indologist who completed her degrees at the University of Delhi and Columbia University. She taught English at Delhi (~1973–1978) and became Class of 1933 Professor and South Asia Institute Director at Columbia University (~1989).

Gaurinath Sastri was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society (~1957–1961), Principal of Sanskrit College and University (~1958–1969), and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1969–1974).
Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. He studied at Elphinstone College (~1885–1887) and under Bhagwanlal Indraji (~1887–1888).
